title: Localized compaction advisor and kernel affinity handshake for paged KV cache
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: We observe tail latency spikes during mixed short/long sequences caused by simultaneous background compaction and hot-path kernel handoffs. Compaction occasionally evicts fragments needed by in-flight prefill windows, forcing kernel fallbacks and decode stalls. Goal: Implement a localized compaction advisor that makes compaction decisions constrained by active prefill horizons and a kernel affinity handshake so the kernel selector is aware of imminent compaction actions. The approach should reduce prefill-induced kernel fallbacks, lower 99.9th percentile latency on small-batch traffic, and avoid regression in throughput for long-sequence workloads. This ticket coordinates design, simulation, and a staged rollout (canary -> region rollouts) with observability hooks for monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor algorithm selects compaction candidates avoiding pages with prefill reservations for at least the next 200ms horizon
Kernel selector exposes an affinity signal (low/medium/high) and honors affinity when fallback cost > measured threshold
End-to-end tests show 25% reduction in 99.9th percentile prefill latency on mixed workload benchmark compared to baseline
No more than 3% throughput regression on long-sequence steady-state benchmark
Canary rollout produces no customer-impacting errors and observability dashboards added for compaction-conflict counts

notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive compaction reduces memory pressure but increases kernel churn; advisor chooses localized, time-bounded deferrals. The kernel affinity handshake keeps selector lightweight (three-level enum) rather than full reservation protocol to minimize RPC surface. Rollout plan includes staged canary with traffic shaping to reproduce mixed workload profile.
